title: Fine-grained Urban Heat Island Effect Forecasting: A Context-aware Thermodynamic Modeling Framework

problem.claim: Accurate urban heat island forecasting is needed to identify high-risk periods and locations, particularly for cities with vulnerable populations.

gap.claim: Existing methods are limited by insufficient data granularity and inadequate modeling of regional thermodynamics, reducing accuracy and spatio-temporal granularity.

contributions.claim: DeepUHI is a data-driven, context-aware framework for modeling local thermodynamics based on the heat equation.
The paper introduces the SeoulTemp multi-modal dataset for street-level urban heat island effect prediction.
DeepUHI is integrated into the SeoUHI platform to provide hourly street-level urban heat island forecasting for Seoul.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments improve accuracy in urban heat island prediction and warning tasks and outperform leading models.
The authors report deploying DeepUHI for hourly street-level urban heat island forecasting in Seoul through the SeoUHI platform.
The authors report that the code, platform, and dataset are accessible through the provided GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Climate change and urbanization intensify the urban heat island effect and its impacts on urban communities.
Fine-grained forecasting is important for identifying high-risk periods and locations, especially for vulnerable populations.
Existing approaches face limitations in data granularity and regional thermodynamic modeling.
DeepUHI combines context-aware heat-equation-based thermodynamic modeling with the SeoulTemp multi-modal street-level dataset and heat decomposition.
The authors report improved prediction and warning accuracy, platform integration for Seoul forecasting, and public access to the implementation and data.

source_observation.claim: The framework represents urban thermodynamics through thermodynamic cycles and thermal flows while integrating urban environmental data.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly structuring domain processes may help connect heterogeneous environmental inputs to fine-grained forecasting.

application.claim: For other spatial forecasting tasks, consider domain-informed decompositions that represent relevant flows or cycles.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this modeling strategy transfers beyond urban heat island forecasting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation metrics, baseline model identities, or numerical performance improvements.
The abstract does not describe the SeoulTemp dataset's size, collection process, modalities, or coverage.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the heat decomposition method or thermodynamic modeling.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported results or repository accessibility.
